newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Hedges pay off as Cisco slides.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Hedges pay off as Cisco slides.

text.p: Downside hedging with options paid off for holders of Cisco Systems shares Wednesday as the stock slid after the company reported fiscal second quarter earnings late Tuesday.
Cisco shares, by far the most active on the Nasdaq market with volume of more than 32.2 million, were down 4-3/8 at 62-3/4 in late trading.
Analysts said the stock was hit by concern over the traditionally weak April quarter as the second quarter profit of $0.51 a share beat analysts' consensus estimate of $0.50.
But some traders said the numbers still fell short of some expectations on Wall Street.
"Everybody saw the $0.51 (earnings per share) number, and it just wasn't that great," one options trader said. "They thought the whisper number was $0.52-$0.54, and said 'Oops.'"
Among the options, which trade on both the Chicago Board Options Exchange and the Pacific Stock Exchange, the February 65 call was most active, with combined volume of about 8,365.
The February 60, 70 and 75 calls were also active, as were the February 60 and 65 puts.
Patrick Hamilton of LETCO said volatilities popped off the opening but quickly dropped back into the mid-40 region and held in that zone for the balance of the trading session.
"I'm not seeing any urgency to sell it off," he said, adding that the options activity was two-way, with put buying not particularly heavy despite the stock's decline.
"It's mostly been people coming in buying the offer and selling the bid," he said.
Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said some investors most likely had sold calls or bought puts ahead of the earnings to hedge stock positions.
"I think there was a lot of hedging going on before the earnings," he said. "Traditionally you buy puts or sell calls. But the sale of a call is only partial protection.
"Those people that buy puts get the full benefit of a decline whereas the ones that sold calls against stock as a hedge have protection limited to the premium," Schwartz said.
